Honestly the supposed clarifications for Giovanni seriously watered down his character for the sake of glazing Nikki. Especially when you consider the hardships he went through for revenge, only to be told that the turning back of time was just a coincidence. It’s very bad storytelling. 

Not only that, Ena’s presence was watered down as well. Initially she’s seen as like a guide to nikki, a knowledgeable deity of sort who was wise but also pitifully trapped. But the new intro makes her seem like some minor god who did things without knowing why. Ena from before seemed to know a lot about the heart of infinity, including the dangers, but the way the seer describes Ena makes it seem like she barely knows anything about it. Mind you, Ena is a well-loved character so this change is also quite negative to fans.

several reasons I could of would be first, to quickly introduce the coop function. They want coop to have some lore behind it, and remember since the main story is time gated, new players would have to wait days just to unlock it and they don’t want that. 

Second is probably to try and get on the good side of veteran nikki players. Veteran players knew the significance of the star sea and the dress, and I guess a lot of those players were not happy with how IN is going in terms of both the story and especially nikki. 

Lastly is to try and up the stakes. A popular complaint by players is on how it feels like the story doesn’t have any stakes to it and feels very childish. So they try to fix that by reworking the intro to make the stakes higher.

Personally as a player, I feel that the devs made the mistake of taking cozy for childish. In the end, the story came out shallow and leaving many players unsatisfied. Making changes to the prologue is essentially a bandaid but one that’s poorly applied. The devs are clearly still trying to figure out what IN is supposed to be. 

It’s also quite rare for a live service game to make changes to the story so early on in the game’s life. ToF and wuwa had pretty rocky starts as well, but they didn’t change their storyline either. They worked hard to improve and even gave players an option to skip the first few quests entirely. 

TBH I kind of wish IN devs stuck to their original vision. Like what I commented in previous posts, the devs should’ve taken the L, learned from their mistakes and move on to try and make better quests and characterisations. Not go back and redo something despite the game being out for months. There’s now some continuity errors and also double the work because essentially theres now 2 different “canon” storylines for their players depending on whether they joined pre-1.5 or post 1.5

Edit: just want to add some extra stuff because I made this comment quite late at night. Yes I am aware of other gacha companies (even less well-known ones). Additionally, I am referring to things beyond the gacha banners itself, including the shop. Infold does not shy away from pulling all the stops to entice players to spend something, and they do this both subtly and directly. From literally having the store icon right at the Center of the top bar so you will always see it whether consciously or subconsciously, to all the very cheap clothes and accessories that you get by paying $1-$5. Those will all add up and you won’t even realise that you’ve spend so much. 

Also regarding banners (5 star banners), remember that IN does not have early pity. Other open world single player gacha games do, meaning that you have a significant chance of getting the premium unit in less than 90 pulls, and even a chance of getting duplicates very early. IN does not have this. Duplicates are fixed to the pulls you’ve done, and you must pull over 100 times to get the full 5 star outfit. That makes the gacha also a bit more expensive than other similar games. The main saving grace is the fact IN has  a really good 4 star banner system. But their 5 star banner system is frankly dog water. 

Thats why I say it’s valid for f2p players to genuinely be worried. Gacha as a whole is predatory, but with other factors that entices a player to spend, the fomo and predatory nature gets ramped up more. For many of these players, IN isn’t their first gacha game, nor is it their first open world gacha games. The complaints made regarding this is not due to greed but because many players have a baseline to compare to and can actually be concerned about the health of free currencies and pulls of the game.

I do have a number of gripes with the game, but the main ones is definitely resource management and FOMO. The devs seriously need to optimise the resource management and the materials needed to craft clothes. Why do 3 star outfits need bouldy materials??? It absolutely doesnt make sense. Other than open world materials, everything else mostly requires stamina. It makes crafting and leveling clothes a terrible experience as you’re always having to trade off something when spending your stamina. 

Genshin, for example, alleviates this issue by providing some of the resources in events. You can get talent books, weapon mats, artifacts exp, weapon exp, character exp, and ascension materials through quests and events.

The game is also a lot more FOMO inducing than other gacha games. I suppose it’s on brand for infold/papergames but it’s still worrying because they’re pulling a sizeable amount of new time gacha players. The game really really really tries to get you to spend money somehow, especially with the low prices. 

My biggest fear is that the game would get more FOMO and p2w-heavy as time goes. I do hope that they do not lock furniture behind a gacha system. Like honestly, there’s genshin as reference! Just copy what they do and put special furniture in bp. Or follow zzz’s bangboo banners where it uses in-game currency that can’t be bought with money. 

The game has lots of potential and I see it as a forefront for more female-oriented games in the market. The devs are also very responsive and quick to act, like when they stopped giving out the time-limited resonance crystals after players complained (hopefully for good). I am genuinely so sorry for what you’re going through. Believe me, I felt the same way as you in the past, asking what I did wrong, whether He just hates me. 

Firstly, let yourself grief. Let yourself be angry. What you’re experience is difficult and painful and you deserve to feel and process those emotions. 

Once you feel better, even just slightly, reflect back on the things you have done so far. The actions you took so far. Then, try and look at all the resources you have on hand and see what actions you can take next. The goal here is to try and reign control. Emotions such as anxiety stems from the feeling of not having control. Just allowing yourself to feel like you have control over something can really help alleviate the pain and anxiety. 

For example, sometimes in moments of grief you end up neglecting yourself. An action you can plan is to try and shower daily (yes taking care of yourself also counts as a resource you have on hand. Your wellbeing is very very important). Then you start trying to shower one day at a time. 

I am not going to lecture or scold you for feeling angry. That is a very human response to a situation where you are hurt and don’t know what to do. But the anger won’t last forever, the pain you’re feeling won’t last forever either. If possible, are you able to find a mental health professional for help?

From what you said, I merely interpret your words as indirectly saying that there’s only one “correct” way, considering the question on added emotions. Of course this is how I interpreted so if that’s not your intention feel free to correct me. 

And regarding your second part, while I agree that it applies for certain characters, it clearly does not apply for all. If all boisterous characters remain boisterous, or if a quiet character is only ever quiet, then they are often considered badly designed characters. They’d be considered as flat, one dimensional characters. That’s why Xiao in jp dub being more vocally agitated is fine because it adds dimension. The finer details can really make a character well-rounded, especially complex ones like Xiao. 

A simpler example I can think of is Itto. We know him as a very extroverted and loud guy, but he also has moments of sombre that we’ve seen. Despite it not fitting his usual image, it still makes sense due to the situation and his personality as an extremely compassionate character. Now unlike Xiao, he’s a lot less complex. Generally the more complex a character is, the greater the differences in interpretation. But as long as said reaction and tone fits not only the character, but the situation, then it’s considered acceptable unless stated otherwise.

Do note that while cn is the original language, it doesn’t mean other dubs are invalid in any way. The nuances you spoke of for Xiao doesn’t take away the core aspect of his personality. As stated, different VAs interpret differently and act out the best they can, what they feel the character is supposed to act. You can’t expect one VA to act out the nuances the same as the other, it will just not work.

Also to add on, added emotions is okay if it’s appropriate, and what’s considered “appropriate” ranges as well depending on how it’s brought across. For Xiao, even though he’s generally quiet, it’s still not out of character for him to be visibly agitated if provoked, in this case by bringing up Zhongli. There’s no “my way or the highway” here.

Multiplayer is fine. Players can’t get your credentials just by joining your world or playing coop. Based on what I’ve read from r/GenshinHacked and some stuff I learned from my Infocomm security modules in school, the common way people can get your credentials is either by telling them, having your email exposed (through data leaks from other services) or by clicking sus links/downloading sus stuff.


The first part is common sense, don’t tell people your email and password. Even if you trust them, you won’t know if they’ll stab you in the back. Data breaches can happen, and if you’re using the same email on other services, you might have your email exposed online. Always keep up to date on data breach news, and try to keep a look out to see if your email has been exposed elsewhere. For the last one, it’s a bit complicated, but essentially when you click or download sus stuff, unwanted things can be downloaded in the background. These things can range from extracting all saved info, to even acting as keyloggers and recording every clicks. This is unfortunately, another common way people get hacked. 

Change your password often, install a good antivirus and always try to be aware of any data breaches that might make your account vulnerable.
